results.name: Parcel_Boundaries_of_Indiana_Current
results.title: Parcel Boundaries of Indiana Current
results.description: This data layer is an Esri file geodatabase polygon feature class that contains parcel boundaries maintained by county agencies in Indiana. It was released by the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO) on February 1, 2022. The IGIO compiled the data as part of the Indiana Data Harvest program between the Indiana Geographic Information Council (IGIC) and all Indiana counties to provide the most accurate framework data for the citizens of Indiana. These layers include address points, street centerlines, land parcels, and governmental boundaries.
results.snippet:
This dataset was developed to provide accurate parcel boundaries for Indiana, as part of Indiana's annual GIS Data harvest Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI) of the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO).

If attempting to download this data in shapefile or file geodatabase format on indianamap.org, please note that this dataset is too large to fit in a shapefile and generating a geodatabase does not perform well in the ArcGIS Hub interface. To download a pre-zipped file geodatabase, please go to https://countydataharvest.in.gov/statewide/2022/DataHarvest_2022_SingleFGDB_20230125.zip.
results.accessInformation: This data set was created as part of the Indiana Geographic Information Office's GIS Data Harvest Program. The source data used to create this dataset was provided by Indiana counties.
results.licenseInfo: CREDIT - It is requested, but not required, that the Indiana GIS Data Harvest Program be cited in any products generated from this data set. If citing, the following source citation language should be included: [Parcel Boundaries of Indiana 2021: Parcel Boundaries Maintained by County Agencies in Indiana, (Indiana Geographic Information Office, File Geodatabase, Polygon Feature Class), 20220201].
results.source: Megan R.L. Compton, Indiana Office of Technology, Indiana Geographic Information Officer

results.title: Reynoldsburg city and schools (master)
results.description:
City of Reynoldsburg
This layer contains all the parcels that make up Reynoldsburg, Ohio: the original village boundaries and all annexations and detachments, from 1839 through November, 2020. It includes both successful and rejected annexations. This layer can be filtered to create different views; for example:
  • all the annexations for a given year
  • all the annexations in a given county
  • all the annexations in a given township
  • all the failed annexations
  • all the pending annexations
This data comes from several sources:

All counties
  • images of the original annexation documents
    • 1839-2019, scans provided by the Office of the City Clerk, Reynoldsburg
    • 2019-2020, images from online City Council meetings
  • BLM National Public Land Survey System 
Franklin County 
  • January 2019 Parcel Feature Archive Annexation, RightOfWay, and RoadCenterline layers, from the Franklin County Auditor and Franklin County Engineer
  • School District Boundary layer, from Franklin County Auditor
Licking County 
  • Parcel map and maps of right-of-ways and centerlines, from the Licking County Auditor.
Fairfield County 
  • Parcel map from the Fairfield County Auditor.
Reynoldsburg City School District
In addition, this layer contains all the parcels that make up the Reynoldsburg City School District, including those that are not part of the City of Reynoldsburg.

Areas of unincorporated Truro and Jefferson Townships that are part of the school district
For these areas, I relied on the "2019 Parcel Archive: Annexations" layer from the Franklin County Auditor. This layer provides the school district for every parcel, including those that are not part of a municipality. 

Areas of unincorporated Etna Township that are part of the school district
I added these shapes by hand, tracing the ones that are completely surrounded by the City of Reynoldsburg, and drawing in the areas bordering the city, with guidance from the Licking County "Parcels_20200117" layer, and the layer "School Districts," created by the Cleveland State University NODIS Center. However, since the "School Districts" layer was created by using voter registration records, and had a statewide focus rather than a Reynoldsburg focus, I did not take it to be definitive (especially since some of its data for Franklin County differed from that provided by the Franklin County Auditor). Where possible, I used current Licking County voter registrations (November 2020) to determine the boundaries. I confirmed the boundaries by using the district transportation document for the 2020-2021 school year.

Areas of unincorporated Violet Township that are part of the school district 
I added these shapes by hand, tracing the ones that are completely surrounded by the City of Reynoldsburg, and drawing in the areas bordering the city, with guidance from the Fairfield County parcels layer, and the layer "School Districts," created by the Cl eveland State University NODIS Center. However, since the "School Districts" layer was created by using voter registration record some of its data for Franklin County differed from that provided by the Franklin County Auditor). This layer is still in progress, as I have been unable to access either Fairfield County Auditor data on school district boundaries or voter registration data. s, and had a statewide focus rather than a Reynoldsburg focus, I did not take it to be definitive (especially since some of its data for Franklin County differed from that provided by the Franklin County Auditor). This layer is still in progress, as I have been unable to access either Fairfield County Auditor data on school district boundaries or voter registration data. I confirmed the boundaries by using the district transportation document for the 2020-2021 school year.

Annexed areas that fell within multiple districts
For each such area, I created a duplicate shape with all the same information about ordinance year, ordinance number, and city; then trimmed each shape to fit the area of one of the school districts and added the relevant district name and code to that shape. I confirmed the boundaries by using the district transportation document for the 2020-2021 school year.

results.description: The RailroadROW feature class contains polyline features representing the edge boundaries of railroad right-of-way corridors in Franklin County, Iowa. These features reflect the general alignment of railroad property used for rail transportation, as recorded in county and state transportation records. The dataset is maintained to support land records management, planning and zoning, transportation studies, and emergency response operations. RailroadROW data also provides an important base layer for integrating transportation networks with parcels, utilities, and roadway infrastructure in the county GIS. results.name: UA_LBRS_Address_Points_Layer
results.title: UA LBRS Address Points Layer
results.description:
LBRS Address points for Franklin County with a 7 mile buffer (of COTA taxing district) showing data pulled from surrounding counties. This file follows the OGRIP/ODOT LBRS specs that can be found here: http://ogrip.oit.ohio.gov/ProjectsInitiatives/LBRS.aspx

The Franklin LBRS file is managed by MORPC but updated by the local communities. For ODOT purposes, MORPC is only responsibe for the Franklin County portion of this file. The data outside of the county boundary is only updated 2x a year to assist municipalities whose boundaries extend outside.
results.snippet: The Address Point layer contains point (XY) locations for all addressable structures. Each point represents a single address. This file is part of the State wide LBRS program to help update ODOTs address inventory and provide accurate and up to date information to local agencies. This particular file is an expansion of the Franklin County area to include cities that extend outside of Franklin. The extended 7 mile buffer of data was pulled from other county files. The collaboration developed by MORPC with the local GIS users will be editing this file and providing periodic updates to ODOT and the public
results.accessInformation: Current editors of the file include:  Columbus, Dublin, Worthington, Westerville, Gahanna, Grove City, Hilliard, Franklin County Engineer, Franklin County Auditor and MORPC
